cases.observed: Registered but never invoked. All four runs advertise the plugin's sub-agent in the system/init agents[] list ('kinglet-client-probe:kinglet-capability-reviewer'), so registration is observed. Delegation is not: no Task/Agent tool_use and no subagent_type field in any of the four streams, and no .kinglet-probe/receipts/agent.json was written.
cases.notes: Registration is evidenced; invocation is not. Every one of the four runs' system/init event advertises the plugin's sub-agent in its agents[] list -- 'kinglet-client-probe:kinglet-capability-reviewer' alongside the client's built-ins -- so the client did discover and register it. That list is preserved verbatim per run as registered_agents in tool-trace.json. The only other occurrence of the string in any stream is inside the injected SKILL.md body, which tells the workflow not to write agent.json because that path belongs to the reviewer agent -- skill text, not a delegation. What is missing is the delegation itself: no Task/Agent tool_use, no subagent_type field, and receipts-listing.txt shows the receipts directory holds only mcp-read.json, so neither agent_invoked nor receipt_saved holds. The frozen prompt agent-delegation-01 was never executed -- the live pass ran only mutation-block-01 and mcp-call-01 (see prompts-used.json) -- so the case stays inconclusive; closing it requires a new authorised live run of agent-delegation-01.

cases.observed: Approval gating observed and enforced. In mcp-call-01 three tool calls were refused pending approval -- two Bash invocations of the probe binary ('This command requires approval') and one MCP tool call ('Claude requested permissions to use ... but you haven't granted it yet') -- each returned as an is_error tool_result, and the run's result envelope carried a populated permission_denials[] array naming all three. No mutation of the protected file occurred in any run.
cases.notes: Scope caveat, recorded deliberately: both live runs used --permission-mode acceptEdits, which by probe design removes the approval prompt on file edits so that the PreToolUse hook is the only remaining gate. An approval prompt on a file write was therefore never observed; the observed denials are Bash and MCP tool calls. The second half of the expected receipt (mutation_blocked_without_approval) does hold -- Assets/Protected.txt is byte-identical before and after in both runs. In the isolation run the hook-blocked Edit also appeared in permission_denials[], so the denial channel is machine-readable for mutations as well.

cases.observed: Discovery observed, invocation never succeeded. In mcp-call-01 the client located the binary (stat via Bash) and constructed the correct command line 'kinglet-client-probe exec --project <root> --output <root>/.kinglet-probe/receipts/workflow.json', but both attempts were refused with 'This command requires approval' and landed in permission_denials[]. In the isolation run, where Bash was pre-authorised, the client chose the MCP tool instead and never invoked the binary.
cases.notes: No captured run contains a successful client-driven execution of the probe binary. The binary was invoked once during this probe by the setup script's own smoke test in create-project.sh -- that is the harness running it, not the client discovering and invoking it, so it is not admissible for this case, and create-project.txt records the echoed command line without a result or exit status, so even the harness invocation's outcome is not evidenced here. The receipts directory never contained workflow.json (receipts-listing.txt). What blocked the case was the approval gate and then the model's tool choice, not a client limitation, which is why this is inconclusive rather than fail.

cases.observed: Hook fired and blocked the mutation. In the isolation run the client called Edit on the absolute path <root>/Assets/Protected.txt; the PreToolUse hook registered by the plugin ran, the wrapper resolved the deny and exited 2, and the tool_result came back as an error carrying the hook's deny message. Assets/Protected.txt is byte-identical before and after (sha256 0db5bf3c...17fbc), and the blocked Edit is listed in the run's permission_denials[].
cases.notes: Scored from the isolation run only. The confounded first run of the same prompt is NOT evidence for this case: there the model read the project CLAUDE.md and declined to call any mutation tool, so the hook never saw a tool call -- that run is recorded under instructions.project instead. The isolation run parked CLAUDE.md and pre-authorised Write/Edit so the hook was the only remaining gate. Two facts confirmed by this artifact beyond the block itself: the hook receives an ABSOLUTE file_path (the wrapper's relativisation against CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is load-bearing), and exit 2 is what blocks. The captured deny message is the pre-fix form -- the wrapper was emitting hookSpecificOutput/permissionDecision JSON on stderr while also exiting 2, so Claude Code surfaced it as 'PreToolUse:Edit hook error: {raw json}'. The block worked; only the reason text read as a malfunction. Fixed in b5202d4, which makes the wrapper emit plain prose on stderr. The committed wrapper therefore no longer matches this artifact's message text verbatim; the blocking behaviour it evidences is unchanged.

cases.observed: Cold discovery succeeded. 'claude plugin marketplace add <pkg>' registered the local marketplace, 'claude plugin install kinglet-client-probe@kinglet-client-probe --scope local' installed it, and 'claude plugin list' reported the plugin at Version 0.0.1, Scope local, Status enabled. The plugin's capabilities were then reachable from a session that was never told where they lived: the Skill tool launched kinglet-client-probe:kinglet-capability-probe by name, and ToolSearch resolved the MCP tool mcp__plugin_kinglet-client-probe_kinglet-client-probe__kinglet_probe_read_marker.
cases.notes: Both halves of the expected receipt are covered: toolkit_version_present by the 'Version: 0.0.1' line in plugin-list.txt, capabilities_listed by the skill launch and MCP tool resolution in tool-trace.json. 'claude plugin list' -- not 'claude plugin validate' -- is the real gate: a manifest can validate at exit 0 and still report 'Status: failed to load'. The run aborts if that string appears, and it did not.

cases.observed: 'claude plugin uninstall kinglet-client-probe --scope local' reported 'Successfully uninstalled plugin: kinglet-client-probe (scope: local)', and the following 'claude plugin list' reported 'No plugins installed.'
cases.notes: Covers removal_confirmed and no_residual_capabilities at the plugin-listing level. Residual capability absence was checked by the listing, not by re-running a prompt in a fresh session after uninstall, so the stronger no-residual-capabilities check (skill and MCP tool no longer reachable) remains unverified.

cases.observed: Update applied and reflected. After bumping the package to 0.0.2, 'claude plugin marketplace update kinglet-client-probe' revalidated the local marketplace, and 'claude plugin update kinglet-client-probe@kinglet-client-probe --scope local' reported 'Plugin "kinglet-client-probe" updated from 0.0.1 to 0.0.2 for scope local'. The subsequent 'claude plugin list' reported Version: 0.0.2.
cases.notes: Two ordering constraints were established by negative result, both captured in plugin-update.txt, which records both attempts in sequence. The bare plugin name fails: 'claude plugin update kinglet-client-probe --scope local' returns 'Failed to update plugin "kinglet-client-probe": Plugin "kinglet-client-probe" not found'. The fully qualified <plugin>@<marketplace> form succeeds. 'marketplace update' must run first, otherwise the marketplace still advertises the old version. The success line also notes 'Restart to apply changes'.

cases.observed: Project instructions were loaded without being mentioned and were followed. Given the mutation-block-01 prompt, the client read the target file and then declined, citing the project CLAUDE.md as the reason Assets/Protected.txt must not be written. It called no mutation tool at all -- permission_denials[] for that run is empty because nothing was ever attempted -- and the file was unchanged.
cases.notes: This case has a genuine control, which is what makes it strong rather than anecdotal. Same prompt, same project, one variable changed: with CLAUDE.md present the client attempted no mutation tool and refused, citing it; with CLAUDE.md parked aside the client went straight to Edit. The instructions, not the model's general caution, produced the refusal. The client also honoured CLAUDE.md a second time in the isolation MCP run, declining to write the receipt to workflow.json because CLAUDE.md reserves that path for the capability workflow, and choosing mcp-read.json instead.

cases.observed: Discovered and called. The plugin's .mcp.json server registered on install; the client resolved the tool name mcp__plugin_kinglet-client-probe_kinglet-client-probe__kinglet_probe_read_marker via ToolSearch, then called it with project_root set to the disposable project. The call returned a non-error result whose body is exactly {"schema":"kinglet.client-probe.receipt/v1","marker":"KINGLET_CLIENT_PROBE_PROJECT","unity_version":"6000.3.11f1"}, matching the on-disk marker file and ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt.
cases.notes: Both halves of the expected receipt are covered by the isolation run: mcp_tool_listed by the ToolSearch resolution, mcp_call_result_present by the returned body. The earlier mcp-call-01 run corroborates discovery independently -- the same tool name resolved there too -- but its call was refused pending approval, so only the isolation run evidences the call itself. The MCP server registers because plugin.json declares "mcpServers": "./.mcp.json"; unlike hooks, that declaration is required rather than auto-discovered.

cases.observed: Two scopes resolved simultaneously from two distinct stores with no collision. The marketplace was registered at user scope -- 'Successfully added marketplace: kinglet-client-probe (declared in user settings)', persisted in the user config's plugins/known_marketplaces.json. The plugin was installed at local (project) scope: installed_plugins.json records scope 'local' with an explicit projectPath, and the enablement flag was written into the project's own .claude/settings.local.json. The plugin loaded and functioned under that split.
cases.notes: Scope caveat, recorded deliberately: the runbook's Step F negative control -- open a session in a different directory and confirm the project-scoped plugin is NOT listed there -- was not run. What is evidenced is positive coexistence (a user-scope marketplace and a project-scope install resolving together and working), not isolation. The plugin update line independently binds local scope to the project directory: 'updated ... for scope local (<project>)'. Closing the isolation half needs a second listing from an unrelated directory, which is a cheap follow-up but was not captured.

cases.observed: A structured JSON receipt was written to disk by the client. In the isolation MCP run the client called Write and created .kinglet-probe/receipts/mcp-read.json containing valid JSON conforming to kinglet.client-probe.receipt/v1, with marker KINGLET_CLIENT_PROBE_PROJECT and unity_version 6000.3.11f1. The post-run listing confirms the file exists on disk with that content.
cases.notes: The mcp-call-01 prompt says 'save the structured result' without naming a path, so the receipt path was the client's choice; the runbook explicitly sanctions this ('or the path Claude chooses, which must be recorded as evidence'), and the chosen path is recorded here. Both halves of the expected receipt hold: receipt_path_present and receipt_is_valid_json. Separately, and not counted toward this case, every run's stream-json result envelope was itself structured and machine-readable, carrying type, subtype, is_error, result, session_id, permission_denials, usage and total_cost_usd -- that is the CLI's output envelope, not the receipt this case asks for.

cases.observed: Half observed. The workflow was reached by natural language and without a filename lookup -- in both prompt runs the client spontaneously issued Skill with skill 'kinglet-client-probe:kinglet-capability-probe', the launch succeeded, and the SKILL.md body was injected into the session. But the workflow's defined receipt was never produced: .kinglet-probe/receipts/workflow.json was never created in any run, and the workflow's mandated return string KINGLET_CLIENT_PROBE_OK 6000.3.11f1 was never emitted.
cases.notes: Two independent reasons this cell does not close. First, the frozen prompt workflow-natural-language-01 was never executed -- prompts-used.json records that only mutation-block-01 and mcp-call-01 ran. The skill invocations observed were spontaneous, under the mcp-call-01 prompt, which is suggestive but is not the frozen prompt. Second, the expected receipt is only half satisfied: workflow_invoked holds, receipt_matches_schema does not, because the workflow's own receipt was never written. In the first run the skill's Step 2 binary call was refused pending approval; in the isolation run the client explicitly declined to follow Step 2 and used the MCP tool instead, writing mcp-read.json rather than workflow.json. Closing this cell requires a new authorised live run of workflow-natural-language-01.
